p.n: An Enemy Is Befriended in Times of Need

body.p:
Now the friend is called a friend precisely for the benefits one hopes to gain from him, and the enemy is called
an enemy for the damage one fears from him: for, when the sensible man hopes to benefit from the enemy, he shows him
friendship; and when he fears harm from a friend, he shows him enmity.

p.n: Young Cattle Only Nurse for a While

body.p:
Don’t you see that the offspring
of animals follow their mothers hoping for their milk, but when that stops flowing they part from them

p.n: Clouds and Rain Come and Go

body.p: Just as clouds gather at a certain hour and disperse at another, pour down at a certain hour and hold off at another,

so the sensible man changes his disposition, as matters alter according to the diverse states of his companions:
he can be at ease at times and reserved at others; open at times and cautious at others.

p.n: Enmity Turns into Friendship in Times of Need

body.p:
And a person might cut off some of the favor that had allied him to his friend and not fear
any evil from him, because the basis of the affair had not been enmity. As for someone towards whom the basic state is enmity
and he strikes up a friendship out of a need that causes him to do so-well, when the the matter which made
this happen goes away, things return to the basic state,

as with water heated with fire: when
it is taken off it, the water turns cold again.

p.n: The Cat Is the Rat's Worst Enemy

body.p: And no enemy is more harmful to me than you.

p.n: The Rat's Need for Friendship Has Gone

body.p:
You and I were compelled
by a matter which had brought us to the agreement we achieved; but the matter
which had made you need me and me you has passed, and I fear that in its passing is
the return of the enmity between me and you.

p.n: The Weak Must Avoid the Strong

body.p:
There is no good in the weak being close to the powerful enemy and no good
in the humble being close to the proud enemy.

p.n: The Cat Desires the Rat for Food

body.p: And I’m not aware that you have any need for me except your wanting to eat me,

so I don’t see any trust in you;
for

p.n: The Cautious Weak Is Better Than Deluded Strong

body.p:
I have learned that the weak person is closer to being safe
from the powerful enemy when he is wary of him and not misled by him, than the powerful who is misled
by the weak and open to him.

The sensible man shows his enemy favor, if he is compelled to it:
he displays friendliness, and shows himself open <>

can hardly be excused for
his misstep;
